physics-based-character-control technique sourced

Learned physics-based character control

Neural policies trained with reinforcement learning drive simulated humanoids by joint torques to imitate motion capture, and MaskedMimic-style controllers accept partial goals such as keyframes, text, or an object to sit on.

Animation & motion2024Researchdeterminism Mitigable4 mechanics affected
this record asyaml sourcemarkdownjson

mechanism

A ragdoll with joint actuators is simulated in a physics engine; a policy network outputs PD targets each step and is trained with RL in massively parallel GPU simulation to track motion capture clips. MaskedMimic first trains a full-body tracker, then distills it into a conditional generative student that receives a masked goal: any subset of future joint positions, a text description, a head and hand signal from VR, a path, or a target object. The same controller therefore handles locomotion, steering, and sitting on varied furniture and transfers flat-ground motions to rough terrain. InterMimic distills per-subject teachers into one student refined by RL for whole-body human-object interaction from imperfect mocap.

limitations

  • Every character needs a physics simulation step plus policy inference, which is costly at the hundreds-of-agents scale colony and management sims use; no crowd-scale runtime figures are published in the cited work.
  • Training requires large mocap datasets and GPU-parallel RL; retargeting to non-human or stylized rigs requires retraining.
  • Physical controllers can fall or jitter in edge cases, which is hard to QA across open-ended situations.

affects

Direct avatar control

The controlled character becomes a physical body that adapts footing to terrain and reacts to pushes, instead of playing canned clips that slide over geometry.

Deepens
affects

Injury body model

With a simulated body, a wound could change gait by limiting joint torque instead of swapping in an authored limp; the cited work does not demonstrate injury-conditioned motion, so this remains a projection.

Enables new form
affects

Rigid-body physics

Characters join the rigid-body simulation as actuated bodies, so carried, pushed, and collided objects affect them and vice versa (InterMimic human-object interaction).

Deepens
affects

Smart objects

When an object advertises an interaction (sit, lie, lean), a goal-conditioned controller can perform it on new furniture geometry without a bespoke animation per object, as MaskedMimic shows for chairs, stools, and sofas.

Cuts authoring cost
builds on

claims

2 with sources
c01high

MaskedMimic (SIGGRAPH Asia 2024) formulates physics-based control as motion inpainting: one controller generates motion from keyframes, text, VR head or hand tracking, paths, or objects, and interacts with chairs, stools, tables, and sofas while transferring to irregular terrain; code is released as ProtoMotions.

src-tessler-2024-maskedmimic

c02medium

InterMimic (2025) trains a single policy for physics-based human-object interaction from hours of imperfect motion capture by distilling subject-specific teacher policies and refining with RL; the authors report zero-shot generalization and compatibility with kinematic motion generators.
